---
title: "Insurance Market Opportunities"
---

## What stands out in the income data?

```{r}
#| label: load-acs-data
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

county_colors <- c(
  "Miami-Dade" = "#0072B2",
  "Broward" = "#E69F00",
  "Palm Beach" = "#009E73"
)

acs_data <- read_csv(
  "data/south-florida-block-groups.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(county = factor(county, levels = names(county_colors)))

income_summary <- acs_data |>
  group_by(county) |>
  summarise(
    median_income = median(median_household_income),
    income_q1 = quantile(median_household_income, 0.25),
    income_q3 = quantile(median_household_income, 0.75),
    median_age = median(median_age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

In these block-group estimates, Palm Beach has the highest median household income (`r scales::dollar(income_summary$median_income[income_summary$county == "Palm Beach"])`), followed by Broward (`r scales::dollar(income_summary$median_income[income_summary$county == "Broward"])`) and Miami-Dade (`r scales::dollar(income_summary$median_income[income_summary$county == "Miami-Dade"])`). The distributions overlap, and each county has block groups spanning a wide income range; county averages alone would hide that local variation.

```{r}
#| label: county-income-distributions
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-alt: "Three county panels compare the distributions of block-group median household income; dashed lines mark each county's median."

ggplot(
  acs_data,
  aes(
    x = median_household_income,
    color = county,
    fill = county
  )
) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(
    data = income_summary,
    aes(xintercept = median_income),
    color = "#333333",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(county), ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = county_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = county_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k", accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Block-group incomes vary within every county",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines mark each county's median block-group estimate",
    x = "Median household income (USD)",
    y = "Relative density",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020–2024 ACS 5-year estimates."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

The chart gives each block group equal weight, so it describes neighborhoods rather than the distribution of individual residents. Median age, population, household counts, renter-occupied units, and home values add useful context: for example, income and housing values may help frame affordability questions, while age and household patterns may suggest different life-stage needs to investigate.

These are clues for further research, **not evidence of insurance purchasing behavior**. Census demographics cannot show who has insurance, what coverage people prefer, or whether anyone will buy a policy; actual demand also depends on prices, risk, eligibility, preferences, and existing coverage.

## Data sources

This analysis uses Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach County block groups from the [2024 ACS 5-year API](https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5.html). The [Census Bureau ACS data page](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/data.html) describes the survey and its estimates. Block groups missing median income or median age were excluded; auxiliary estimates may still be missing.
